editorial: Imagine entering a tennis court where every serve feels like a confession and every rally a reckoning. Coach Tashi turns her former spouse Art into a powerhouse with a devotion that blurs mentorship and manipulation. The quiet moments—Art facing his former best friend and Tashi's own past—feel like a backstage conversation that never overacts. Some early chapters drift, giving the plot a sluggish feel before the ball finally lands. If you savor emotionally packed sports dramas that linger long after the final serve, this will stay with you.
targetAudience: Ideal for sports fans and character-driven drama enthusiasts.
